title: Gabon After Oil: The Blue Bond, the Manganese Ban and a Rising Debt Bill | The Six, Ep. 18
lede: Gabon pumped 370,000 barrels of oil a day at its 1997 peak; last year it averaged about 240,000. In 2023 it swapped $500 million of debt for ocean conservation at a far lower rate than it pays today, and it is now trying to process its manganese at home while it negotiates with the IMF.
keyPoints: Oil made up 65.5% of Gabon's exports in 2024; oil, manganese and wood together made up 97% (World Bank, Gabon Economic Update 2025).

In August 2023 Gabon bought back $500 million of bonds for $436 million, financed by a US-insured blue bond with a 6.097% coupon. The expected savings, about $163 million over 15 years, fund ocean conservation (The Nature Conservancy; Reuters).

In July 2026 Gabon sold a $920 million, seven-year Eurobond at 9.375% (Ecofin). IMF staff projected public debt rising from 70.9% of GDP in 2024 to 94.3% in 2027; a government audit that rebased GDP puts end-2025 debt at 68.9% (allAfrica; Financial Afrik).

Gabon, the world's second-largest manganese producer, plans to ban raw manganese exports from Jan. 1, 2029 (AFP). Eramet aims to process up to 700,000 tonnes of ore a year in Gabon by end-2031, against forecast 2026 output of about 9.4 million tonnes (Eramet; Financial Afrik).
